summary: Vitus Angermeier is an Indologist who completed his MA under Karin Preisendanz by 2007. He also studied under Chlodwig H. Werba and Roque Mesquita.

Vladimir Tikhonov is a scholar of history, archaeology, Buddhist studies, and religious studies. He studied at St. Petersburg University, Korea University, and under Mikhail Nikolaevich Pak, Kwang Cho, and Chul-hwan Chung, becoming a professor at the University of Oslo circa 2000.

Vladimir Vyacheslavovich Balabushevich (1900–1970) was a scholar of Indology, history, and archaeology. He served as Head of the Indian Department at the Institute of Oriental Studies of the Russian Academy of Sciences, attested in 1970 and 1990.
Volkbert Näther is an Indologist who earned his doctoral degree at the University of Marburg (attested 1975) under the supervision of Claus Vogel.

Tibetologist Volker Caumanns earned an MA at the University of Hamburg (under David P. Jackson) and a PhD at LMU Munich (under Franz-Karl Ehrhard). He worked at LMU Munich, Lumbini International Research Institute, and the University of Bern.

Volker Grabowsky is a historian and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at the University of Kiel. He held positions at the University of Passau, University of Hamburg, National University of Laos, and as Professor at the University of Münster (circa 1999–2007).
W. F. Jayasuriya is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied under Rerukane Ariyaratne (attested 1963), H. D. Dharmasiriwardhana, and M. U. Sri Kaveeswara.
W. H. D. Rouse (1863–1950) was a scholar of Indology and Buddhist studies. He was educated at Cheltenham College and Christ's College, Cambridge (circa 1882–1886).

W. H. R. Rivers (1864–1922) studied at Tonbridge School, Barts and The London School of Medicine, University of London, and St John's College, Cambridge. He held posts at University College London (circa 1893–1897) and the University of Cambridge (circa 1897–1922).

W. Norman Brown (1892–1975) was an Indologist and historian. Educated at Hiram College and Johns Hopkins University under Maurice Bloomfield and Franklin Edgerton, he served as a professor at the University of Pennsylvania (attested 1969–1973).

W. Randolph Kloetzli is a scholar of religious studies, Indology, and Buddhist studies. He earned his PhD at the University of Chicago (1964) under numerous teachers and lectured at American University, George Washington University, and Dartmouth College.

W. S. Karunaratne (1928–1986) was a scholar of Buddhist studies and philosophy. Educated at Dharmaraja, Ananda, and Ceylon colleges, he earned a PhD from the University of London and served as Dean of Oriental Studies at the University of Ceylon (1952–1973).

W. S. Karunatillake was a scholar of linguistics, Indology, and Buddhist studies. He served as a professor at the University of Kelaniya (attested 1997) and was Visiting Numata Professor of Buddhist Studies at Harvard University in 1998.

Wai-lun Tam specializes in religious studies, sinology, and Buddhist studies. He earned his PhD at McMaster University under Koichi Shinohara (attested 1996) and became a professor and department chairperson at The Chinese University of Hong Kong (attested 2016).

Walpola Rahula (1907–1997) was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at the universities of Ceylon, Calcutta, and Paris, under G. P. Malalasekera and Paul Demiéville. He held an appointment at the University of Oxford (circa 1977–1980).

Walter Eugene Clark (1881–1960) was a scholar of Indology, Tibetology, and Buddhist studies who studied at Harvard University. He taught at the University of Chicago (1923–1927) and served as Wales Professor of Sanskrit at Harvard (1927–1950).

Walter Ewer (1784–1863) worked in the fields of history, archaeology, and Indology. He studied at Fort William College (circa 1803–1805) and served in the Indian Civil Service from circa 1803 to 1840.

Walter Liebenthal (1886–1982) was a scholar of Buddhist studies, sinology, and Indology. He held academic posts at Visva-Bharati University as a visiting professor (circa 1952–1959), the University of Tübingen (circa 1960–1965), and the University of Paris.

Walter M. Spink (1928–2019) was a scholar of history, archaeology, Indology, and Buddhist studies. He studied at Amherst College and held posts at Brandeis University (circa 1956–1961) and as Professor at the University of Michigan (attested 2005).

Walter Simon (1893–1981) was a sinologist, Tibetologist, and linguist. He studied at Humboldt University of Berlin under Otto Franke, where he later taught. Simon subsequently held posts at the University of London and SOAS (circa 1936–1960).
